entries.source: Set the top-left corner of this image on the output canvas. X and Y are whole pixels, starting at zero. Other images keep their current positions. Overlap is allowed here; images imported later are drawn on top. The canvas expands to include all placed images. Crops and sizes stay unchanged.

entries.backtranslation: On the drawing place for the image to be output, please place the corner that is both at the upper edge of this image and at the left side of this image. X and Y are numbers chosen from “0, 1, 2, 3, …”; count in pixels starting from zero. The placement locations of other images are not changed. Here, it is all right to put images over one another; images brought in afterward are drawn on the surface of images brought in earlier. So that all placed images are inside the drawing place, the drawing place becomes bigger. The cut/crop locations and image sizes are not changed.

connected_anchor_analysis.candidate_anchor: tan noka tuyka ta ka tan noka harkisama ta ka an sikkew
connected_anchor_analysis.parse: [[[tan noka] tuyka ta] ka [[tan noka] harkisama ta] ka an] sikkew
connected_anchor_analysis.literal_reading: the corner that is both at this image’s upper edge and at this image’s left side
binding_checks: Each directional relational noun has its own immediately preceding, identical tan noka referent. The output drawing-place NP is outside this relative and is not an omitted possessor of either direction.
Both complete locative phrases occur before the single an predicate. They are coordinated as locations of the same singular subject, whose relative-clause head is sikkew.

There is no directional noun after an that could be the nearer head of only the left-side modifier. There is no post-head pe apposition or comma separating a left-side fragment from a supposedly upper corner.

The conceptual-form sikkew removes an unexpressed possessive dependency. Its restrictive relative identifies the geometric intersection corner of the image’s upper and left boundaries in the rectangular image context.
The complete corner NP is the object of anu yan. The output-canvas locative continues to specify where it is placed, rather than which image owns the directional boundaries.
connected_anchor_analysis.semantic_model: For the current rectangular image I, choose the corner c satisfying At(c, upper-edge(I)) AND At(c, left-side(I)); place c on the output drawing area. The singular shared relative does not instruct placing two corners, changing another image, or aligning with the canvas’s own top-left.
connected_anchor_analysis.evidence_vs_inference: Primary sources support the constituent grammar and meanings. The joint two-location relative and its application to rectangular image geometry are the author’s compositional analysis. This is stronger than a word-match list, but it remains a proposal for independent whole-value review.

remaining_uncertainty: Independent linguistic approval is still required for the complete paragraphs and the shared-head additive-locative reading. The author does not turn the earlier local-clause acceptances or this token pairing into whole-value approval.

No exact historical attestation of the new two-location image-corner phrase was found or required. Its legitimacy rests on productive syntax plus the constrained rectangular-image context, rather than a claim of an established technical expression.

Generic sikkew is tied to the image through both geometric restrictions, rather than a direct possessed-head construction. The reviewer should judge that intersection reading in the full instruction and reject it if a genuine competing target-language reading remains.
The repeated explicit tan noka is deliberately conservative and may be less idiomatic than a native speaker’s shorter choice. No native-speaker or community-standard certification is available.
Previously disclosed technical extensions for drawing place, image import/export, numeric domain, pixel units and size remain unchanged. They are not newly validated by this author’s anchor repair.
No runtime, line-wrap, font or rendering test was run, because only draft candidates were authorized in this task.
